title: Matchmakers Are Beating the Dating Recession
author: Ezra Seplowitz
content:
![Matchmakers Are Beating the Dating
Recession](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/10/GettyImages-169365107.jpg)

America is in the midst of a [_dating
recession_](https://ifstudies.org/report-brief/state-of-our-unions-2026-the-
dating-recession?ref=compactmag.com). Almost two-thirds of young adults aren't
dating anyone seriously. But our friends stand apart. Nearly all of them are
dating or happily married. It isn't because they are uniquely attractive,
socially adept, or prosperous. So what is the reason for their success? The
answer is that our community--Orthodox Judaism--is heavily involved in making
it easy for young adults to find their way to the
[__chuppah__](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/476806/jewish/Chuppah-
The-Bridal-Canopy.htm?ref=compactmag.com), the Jewish wedding canopy.

Every few weeks, I, Ezra, along with my wife and several other young-couple
friends, get together to discuss
[__shidduchim__](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/3716771/jewish/The-
Shidduch-How-Jewish-Dating-Works.htm?ref=compactmag.com)--the Hebrew term for
matchmaking. We order dinner, sit around the table, and talk about setting up
our friends. Everyone comes prepared with a list of friends who are looking
for a spouse, along with some basic biographical information: professional
aspirations, personality and interests, and family background. We don't
conclude the meeting until we have thought of ten potential matches. Many of
the ideas don't pan out, but we've had our successes--including several
marriages. This _shidduchim_ group isn't an outlier within the Orthodox Jewish
community. These small groups are commonplace, and our community also sponsors
robust initiatives such as [_YU
Connects_](https://yuconnects.com/?ref=compactmag.com) and [_Ambassadors of
the Heart_](https://en.shagririm.org.il/?ref=compactmag.com).

In fact, I was set up with my wife, Leora, through friends of my parents who
thought it would be a good match and encouraged me to date her. While I was
still engrossed in my undergraduate studies, friends of my mother would pitch
ideas of potential matches, and Leora's name was mentioned several times. This
type of networking among mothers whose children are of marriageable age is
commonplace in Orthodox Jewish communities.
